KEY MESSAGE 1...

Mid and high level clouds will continue to overspread the area 
heading into the evening hours. Low level dry air is in place, with 
dew points in the 40s around the region. Initially any radar returns 
will likely be virga (not reaching the ground) but after sunset some 
sprinkles and light showers will begin to spread in from the west.

The steadier rainfall looks to develop after midnight and overspread 
the forecast area during the predawn hours Sunday morning. Rainfall 
amounts by daybreak are expected to range from a quarter to half inch 
across Central NY and NE PA. The surface low center is forecast to 
track across New York state through the day on Sunday. Most of the 
surface based instability is progged to stay south of our area, 
across south-central PA. With that said, there could be a few 
elevated thunderstorms mainly during the day on Sunday; especially 
from the Twin Tiers south into NE PA. There remains discrepancies in 
the latest CAMs on exactly when and where the steadiest rainfall 
will develop. There appears to be 2-3 rounds of rain tonight through 
early Sunday evening , with some minor breaks of just drizzle and 
light showers in between. PWATs are elevated between 1.5 to 1.8 
inches during this rainfall event, but as mentioned above 
instability looks very limited. This should keep rainfall rates 
down, to generally just a steady rainfall...with only a very low, 
marginal risk for any localized excessive rainfall. This potential 
is mainly confined to NE PA and the Twin Tiers, closer to the modest 
instability over south-central PA. Overall rainfall totals are 
forecast to be between 0.50 to 1.75 inches by the time the rain ends 
Sunday evening.

With the clouds overspreading the area tonight it will remain mild, 
with lows mainly in the 50s expected. Southeast winds increase 
between 7-15 mph with a few higher gusts possible overnight and into 
Sunday morning. The center of the low passes along or just south of 
I-90 in Central NY on Sunday. Winds will become variable as the low 
passes overhead, then turn northwest and increase late in the day. 
Just ahead of the low our area will get into a quasi-warm sector, 
and with dew points pushing up into the 60s it will become slightly 
humid. Despite overcast conditions (and rain showers) all day it 
does look like the warm/moist air advection will push high 
temperature up into the 60s across the region.

Behind the departing low, winds turn northerly overnight and 
gradually diminish. A very dry air mass will advect into the area 
from Canada late Sunday night into Monday. While there could be some 
patchy fog, it will most likely dissipate as drier air mixes down 
toward the surface. PWATs fall to under 0.50 inches for CNY by 
Monday morning, but could remain elevated near 1.25 inches in the 
Wyoming Valley. Overnight lows will be quite cool, dropping into the 
40s to low 50s areawide.

KEY MESSAGE 2...

Drier air continues to advect into the area from the north (from 
700mb down to the surface) through the day on Monday. However, the 
next shortwave will roll east along the stalled front from western 
PA to Central PA by late Monday. This may begin to push some 
additional moisture north as surface winds try to come around out of 
the east-northeast across the Poconos. The most likely scenario is 
that any rain remains south of I-80 in PA though. Clouds will be 
thickest and most widespread over NE PA, fading to mainly sunny 
conditions north along the I-90 corridor of CNY. Expect a steady 
northeast wind between 6 to 15 mph with a few gusts around 20 mph 
through the day. Temperatures will be seasonable in the 60s for highs.

The most uncertainty in the medium range forecast comes Monday night 
into Tuesday. The aforementioned mid level wave moves slowly east 
across PA and the northern Mid-Atlantic in this time period. Model 
differences remain in regards to the northern extent of deeper mid 
level moisture and potential rain. The 12z GFS remains further north 
and would spread steady rain across all of NE and CNY north to the 
US Route 20 corridor...and it doesn't shift the rain south until 
Tuesday evening. Meanwhile the 12z NAM brings scattered showers 
north to the NY/PA border area Tuesday morning, but keeps it dry 
further north. The ECMWF is similar to, if not slightly further 
south than the NAM. There will be big forecast implications 
depending on where this rainfall sets up; as the cool easterly flow 
in the low levels could lock in and keep temperatures very cool 
(upper 40s to mid-50s) where the rain does setup. Meanwhile to the 
north and east of the rain it would be partly sunny and milder with 
temperatures in the low to mid-60s. Considering the high amount of 
spread and uncertainty in the guidance, the official forecast used 
the blended ensemble guidance, which brings a few showers southern
